items.q: Did GLM 5.2 earn the BridgeMind stamp of approval?
items.a: **No** — despite strong BridgeBench scores. Fast and cheap on paper, but fails **attention to detail** on interactive builds and hits **brutal rate limits** on the **$65/mo** GLM coding plan.

items.q: Why did ZAI time the GLM 5.2 drop this way?
items.a: Same-day as the US **Fable 5 / Mythos 5 ban** — marketed as "open AI belongs to the people," exclusive to coding-plan users (not chatbot/API at test time). Plan price had doubled from ~**$35 → $65/mo**.

items.q: What broke in the interactive game tests?
items.a: Horror house: third-key never spawns hunter; door won't open. Stealth: **pitch-black**, unplayable. Minecraft clone: UI loads but **player cannot move**. Remotion video: generic purple + weak copy.

items.q: What's the Chinese open-model pattern BridgeMind sees?
items.a: Strong on **isolated HTML demos** (Flappy Bird, thunderstorm, coral reef), weak on **end-to-end game logic**. Contrast: pre-ban Fable 5 one-shot perfection on the same horror-house prompt.
**#1 reasoning** (+1.3% over Fable 5); first **100% BS** score (5.1 was ~26%); **#6 hallucination**, **#4 refactoring**, **86.6 debugging**; **296 tok/s** (~3.5× GLM 5.1).
**#1 reasoning** in the same session as **broken Minecraft movement**. Trust bar: "If you can't navigate a voxel map, I won't trust you with subscribers on the line."

items.q: How fast does the coding plan burn under multi-agent load?
items.a: ~1 hour with **5–9 subagents** → **71% of 5-hour quota** and **14% of weekly** on ~37M tokens — incompatible with real multi-agent vibe coding despite ~**$1/M** input pricing.

items.q: Is there any niche for GLM 5.2?
items.a: Maybe **Hermes-style background orchestration** (cheap + fast + strong reasoning/BS) — **not** as primary IDE agent for interactive greenfield.
